title: Collect and act on user feedback continuously
summary: Numbers tell you what is happening; feedback tells you why. Set up regular ways to hear from users and make sure what they say reaches decisions.

beginner: List where feedback already arrives: support tickets, reviews, surveys, sales calls and social media.
Add a simple way to give feedback inside the product if there is not one.
Once a week, read a sample and group it into themes.
Share the top themes with the team, with real quotes.
Link themes to backlog items and tell users when you fix something they raised.
intermediate: Bring feedback from all channels into one place.
Tag and theme it weekly, with counts.
Share top themes and link them to backlog decisions.
experienced: Combine feedback with behaviour data to size each theme.
Watch for groups whose feedback is under-represented.
Run regular satisfaction measures and track them alongside usage.
Make feedback review part of planning, not an extra.

canDelegateTo.task: Theme feedback and run follow-up interviews

toolExamples.jira: Link feedback themes to backlog items so you can see what drove each change.
toolExamples.notion: Keep a feedback database tagged by theme, source and user type.
toolExamples.miro: Run a monthly affinity mapping session on recent feedback.
toolExamples.claude: Paste anonymised feedback and ask it to suggest themes with counts. Check the themes against the raw text.

definitionOfDone: Feedback channels mapped and gathered in one place
pitfalls: Only listening to the loudest users

sources.title: Measuring the user experience on a large scale: the HEART framework (Google Research)
